input.quote: (c) To the extent that Contractor incorporates any of Contractor's Information into the Works, Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.
input.rationale: Section 4 runs in our favour and meets the fallback on its material terms, indeed most of the preferred position. The Works (all work product required by a Statement of Work) "are the property of Company" once invoiced and paid (p0017), and on termination Contractor "hereby assigns to Company, all right, title and interest to any Works in progress" (p0033), so ownership of deliverables vests in Clear Capital rather than being licensed. Contractor retains only its own pre-existing proprietary works, tools, methodologies and know-how not created for us (p0020) — the permitted vendor-retention carve-out — and where that material is embedded in the Works we hold a royalty-free, perpetual, sublicensable licence to use, copy, modify and create derivatives for our business operations (p0021), reinforced by our post-payment/post-termination right to modify the software and engage others to do so without further payment (p0022). No joint ownership is created, no Clear Capital IP or data is assigned to Contractor, and there is no standing vendor licence in our data: Confidential Information (including our records, data and reports) may not be used or disclosed by Contractor without our express prior written permission (p0040), so the Customer-Data element is satisfied by prohibition rather than an over-broad processing licence. Sub-preferred points noted but not redlined: the embedded-IP licence is not expressly labelled "irrevocable" or "worldwide" (it is perpetual and untethered to any revocation or territorial mechanic elsewhere in the Agreement), there is no affirmative sentence confirming we retain all rights in our data, and §4(b)(ii) limits resale/use of Contractor's administrative records to the software we receive. These are wording gaps short of the preferred position, not material failures, so we accept the clause as drafted.
